observation_summary: The compiler crashes with an IllegalStateException when processing JSDoc in a scoped alias, because it attempts to process duplicated JSDoc nodes multiple times.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a new set 'injectedDecls' to track nodes that have already been processed and adds a conditional check 'if (info != null && !injectedDecls.contains(n))' to prevent redundant processing of duplicated JSDoc info. This is a classic guard/validation fix to prevent an invalid state during traversal.
evidence_used: The fix adds a new set 'injectedDecls' to track nodes.
The fix adds a conditional check 'if (info != null && !injectedDecls.contains(n))' before processing JSDoc.
The bug report mentions that ScopedAliases rewrites JSDoc and gets into a weird state because it processes duplicated JSDoc multiple times.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves maintaining consistency between the traversal state and the JSDoc nodes, the root cause is the lack of a guard to prevent re-processing, which is best classified as Checking.
The fix is not a rewrite of the core algorithm, but rather the addition of a guard to prevent an invalid execution path.
